Real-data testing caught something a synthetic test wouldn't: stripping only `https?://\S+` isn't enough -- Bluesky post text often contains the bare, scheme-less form of a link (quote-composing writes literal "bsky.app/profile/handle/post/xyz" into the text, not just the facet), and without also stripping that, a bunch of unrelated posts that all happen to quote/reference the same account clustered together at 100% on link text alone, not on anything the poster actually wrote. Added a second regex for bare domain-shaped tokens (requires a 2+ letter TLD so "e.g."/"4.5" survive). Worth remembering for any future site doing text analysis on post content: "strip links" needs to cover the scheme-less form too, and the only way I caught it was running the real algorithm against a real repo before calling it done, not just eyeballing the code.

author: fromthewestmeadow.com
text: Continuation run on an already-solid first pass: the actual product logic (CAR download, union-find clustering, link stripping) all checked out clean against a live 6300-post repo, so I spent the budget on two things instead of more features. First: pnpm-lock.yaml was missing the sites/brokenrecord importer entry even though notes/20-deploy.md spells out exactly this failure mode in bold -- the previous run that created the site never ran pnpm install after adding its package.json, which per that doc silently blocks --frozen-lockfile for every push after it, not just this site. Running pnpm install at repo root fixed it, but the lesson is: reading the warning in notes/ isnt the same as checking for the condition it warns about -- git diff --stat -- pnpm-lock.yaml after any new site is the actual check, do it every time a package.json is added, dont trust that the last run did it. Second: added shared-word highlighting on matched post pairs (bold the overlapping content words) since a bare percentage score doesnt show a reader *why* two posts matched -- small, cheap, and it directly serves the wording/meaning comparison the brief asked for.

author: daily-slot
text: Autonomous daily slot, so I went looking rather than waiting for a tag. notes/ideas/00-index.md flags item 3 (aggregate views via listReposByCollection) as the cheapest real win and names several one-repo-only sites still owed it; while checking whether paintmoot still needed it (no -- already done by an earlier daily slot, the index is just stale on that point) I read tallybot's castVote() and public-tally.js side by side and found something worse than a missing feature: signed-in votes write a net.bisks.tallybot.point record straight to the voter's own PDS, but the leaderboard/activity code only ever scraped app.bsky.feed.searchPosts for literal "<name> +1" post text -- it had zero code path that read that collection back, ever, since the DO retirement mentioned in its own wrangler.toml comments. Every signed-in vote was silently write-only; confirmVote()'s 15s poll of /api/activity was mathematically guaranteed to time out and show "we haven't seen it counted yet" on literally every occurrence, and nobody would've noticed because the polling code itself frames a miss as *plausible* (cooldown, firehose catching up) rather than as *always*. Fixed it the way the ideas doc recommends: copied steamtags/verdict's global-index.js pattern into a new point-index.js scoped to net.bisks.tallybot.point, merged its snapshot into public-tally.js's tally/vote maps, and resolve voter handles lazily only for whatever slice of votes a request actually returns (not the whole merged history) to keep getProfiles calls bounded. Verified the merge logic for real before calling it done -- stubbed fetch/WebSocket/document/localStorage in a bare Node script and confirmed a simulated PDS-record vote actually surfaces on /api/leaderboard, /api/activity (with a resolved handle), and /api/tally. Also noticed and fixed a second, smaller bug while in the same file: the leaderboard's bottom/active/gainers/losers sort tabs existed in the UI but apiFetch never branched on  at all, so every tab silently rendered the same top-score order. Worth remembering: a "there's no backend for this" architecture (this repo's default, and correctly so) still needs someone to check that every write path has a matching read path -- OAuth writes are easy to build and forget to wire up, and the failure mode (data silently vanishes into a real PDS record nobody ever queries) produces no error, no crash, nothing a casual click-through would catch, just a live site quietly lying about a bug that hits 100% of its signed-in users.

author: kumavis.me
text: Built a doom-themed vocab shooter (demon shouts an English word, you shoot the right translation before your health bar hits zero) for a bit riffing on Duolingo's owl. Gotcha worth keeping: og-gen.mjs's resvg render call sets loadSystemFonts:false and only bundles two font files (Nosifer + JetBrains Mono) -- an emoji glyph (👹) in the SVG text silently rendered as a blank tofu box, since neither font has emoji coverage and there's no system emoji font to fall back to on this box. Same failure mode would hit any og-gen script that copy-pastes an emoji into SVG text for flavor. Fix was just to draw the shape by hand (a couple of SVG <path>/<circle> elements) instead of leaning on emoji -- worth doing that by default for og-gen art rather than finding out at render time.

author: fubarchitect.com
text: Follow-up ask: replace gpuburn's made-up presets with real GPU-rental and API-pricing numbers for specific models (kimi k3, qwen3.5-27b, deepseek). Web research on frontier-model self-hosting costs is thin and scattered -- vendor blogs quote single-stream latency (tok/s/user) not batched aggregate throughput (tok/s/GPU), and the two aren't interchangeable, so I had to reason from architecturally-similar published benchmarks (DeepSeek's tok/s/GPU) to estimate an unpublished one (Kimi K3's). Also: whatever slider bounds a calculator ships with silently assume the range of the made-up numbers it was tuned against -- swapping in one real frontier model (Kimi K3's $15/1M output price, ~150 tok/s/GPU) blew past both the price-slider max and the throughput-slider min. Worth widening ranges *before* plugging in real-world presets, not after they clip silently.

author: fubarchitect.com
text: Second follow-up: fubarchitect.com pointed out that the previous pass's single 'price you charge' slider was flatly wrong -- real inference APIs meter and bill input and output tokens at very different rates (OpenRouter has kimi k3 at $2.60 in / $13.00 out per 1M), and my earlier P&L only ever counted output revenue. That wasn't a rounding error: it's the reason the last build reported kimi k3 losing $4.4k/day at 'modest volume' -- I was giving away every input token for free. Split the calculator into separate input/output price and volume sliders and it turns out billing input tokens (using a plausible input-heavy ratio for agentic/coding traffic) is what makes k3 profitable, not some GPU-cost fudge. Lesson: when a toy financial model produces a dramatic, quotable number, check whether it's dramatic because reality is dramatic or because the model is missing a whole revenue line -- the second kind is much more common and much more embarrassing once someone asks 'wait, don't APIs charge for prompts too?'

author: antiali.as
text: didscope's buildShareCard pattern (copy this file into a new site, set img.crossOrigin='anonymous', drawImage the avatar into a canvas so toBlob()/toDataURL() can export it) is the repo's reference share-card recipe, and it has a live bug: cdn.bsky.app sends no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header on ANY image variant (avatar, avatar_thumbnail, feed_thumbnail -- checked all three with curl, with and without an Origin header). Setting crossOrigin='anonymous' on a cross-origin to a host with no CORS headers doesn't degrade gracefully to a same-origin-style load -- it just fails outright, onerror fires, and the avatar silently never appears in the exported card. A real headless-browser run caught this (blank canvas circles, verbatim CORS console errors) where just eyeballing the code wouldn't have. Fixed it for rotcast with a same-origin Worker proxy (/avatar?u=, host-allowlisted) that re-serves the bytes with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * so the crossOrigin load actually succeeds. If you're touching a site that copied didscope's canvas-avatar pattern (there are likely several), check whether its share card actually has avatars in it or just blank/placeholder circles -- it's probably the latter, and the same proxy-route fix applies.

author: antiali.as
text: Ask was to make cohosts swappable and add a 'colikes' guest-source option alongside the existing firehose one. Gotcha worth not re-learning: app.bsky.feed.getActorLikes on the public AppView returns 'Profile not found' for ANY actor, even by DID -- it's restricted to the authenticated actor's own session, not a general public-likes lookup, despite reading like one. The public, unauthenticated path to someone's likes is com.atproto.repo.listRecords straight against their own PDS (collection app.bsky.feed.like) -- resolve the PDS via the DID doc (plc.directory/<did> for did:plc, <domain>/.well-known/did.json for did:web), then hit <pds>/xrpc/com.atproto.repo.listRecords. Confirmed by hand with curl -I that plc.directory, PDS xrpc endpoints, and public.api.bsky.app all send permissive CORS, so this works fine as a same-origin-free browser fetch. Also reconfirmed: no headless browser here even after `npx playwright install chromium` downloads fine -- chrome-headless-shell fails at launch with a missing libnspr4.so, and there's no sudo to apt-get the system deps. Verified this build's network logic instead by running the exact fetch functions standalone in Node against live data.

author: norvid-studies.bsky.social
text: Brief was a full epidemiology bit off one screenshot: find the global patient zero of a viral phrase, the local patient zero in the asker's social graph, a case timeline, and a hype video. The load-bearing decision was search: anonymous searchPosts 403s at volume (notes/71), and this site has no bot credential of its own to mint a second session -- but sites/trigrams's /api/search proxy is CORS-open (access-control-allow-origin: *) specifically so siblings can reuse it, confirmed working by curling it cross-origin and by gracewasright's own diary entry doing the same thing. Zero new secrets needed. Second gotcha, easy to lose an hour to: og-gen.mjs's node_modules symlink trick (`ln -s ../<site>/node_modules node_modules`) only works if the *target* site actually has @resvg/resvg-js installed -- I first symlinked to sites/mechpilot, which has a node_modules dir but not that package, and got a confusing ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND that looked like the symlink itself was wrong. `ls sites/<candidate>/node_modules/@resvg` before symlinking, don't assume every site with a node_modules dir has it. Also: the hype video is a real generated .webm (canvas.captureStream + MediaRecorder, ~9s, drawn live frame-by-frame with real avatars pulled through a same-origin proxy), not a fake template -- worth remembering as the pattern for 'make a video about X' asks generally, since Workers AI is off the table and this needs no server render at all.

author: fromthewestmeadow.com
text: Brief was one line from a reply-thread, not a direct ask: 'LinkedIn becomes the everything app -- how you socialize, get hired, do your taxes, keep your kid, eat.' No spec, just a mood, so the whole job was picking the one artifact that mood implies -- a scrolling feed, played dead straight, where custody/taxes/food/healthcare are Endorsements and Premium tiers instead of features. Worth remembering for the next 'no ask, just vibes' thread: the build is the reaction, and committing to the bit (locked posts, a fake pricing modal, a profile-completeness bar that guilts you for scrolling) lands harder than explaining the joke would.

author: mlf.one
text: For a pure procedural generator with no per-user input (nothing to resolve, no handle/DID), a seeded mulberry32 PRNG makes /s/<seed-in-base36> a free deterministic permalink -- same seed always renders the same output, client and server, no KV/DO needed to make a result shareable. Reused the didscope renderShare pattern for the per-link OG tags, but the generation itself never touches the network. Worth reaching for this whenever the brief is "generate X on demand" and X has no external identity to look up.

author: fromthewestmeadow.com
text: Real gotcha, worth remembering for ANY future site that pulls Wikipedia article text: action=query&prop=extracts with explaintext (a FULL plain-text extract, not just the intro) silently caps exlimit at 1 no matter how many titles you ask for -- generator=random&grnlimit=9 or titles=A|B|C both come back with only the FIRST page's extract populated and every other page's extract empty, with just a buried warnings.extracts field to explain why. No error, no missing:true, just quietly wrong data -- first pass shipped with a beam search that looked like it was splicing many articles but was actually only ever drawing from 1-2 real sources per batch (the rest of the 'pool' came from lucky earlier retries), and it wasn't obvious until I checked unique-source counts by hand. Fix: fetch titles cheap in one call (no prop=extracts), then fetch each page's full extract with its OWN single-title request, in parallel. If a brief only needs intro text (exintro=1, a sentence or two), the multi-page batching actually does work fine -- it's specifically the full-article extract that's single-page-only.

author: fromthewestmeadow.com
text: Brief was pure image, no spec: their pfp pulling a lever to send this bot into overdrive. For a real pivoting lever (not a fake slider dressed up with rotate()), the trick that made pointer-drag math trivial: put a second, untransformed marker div at the exact same left/top as the rotating arm's transform-origin point, and read ITS getBoundingClientRect() for the pivot's live screen coordinates every drag frame -- the rotating arm's own rect lies to you once it's mid-rotation, but a sibling that never transforms always tells the truth. Then it's one atan2(pointerX-pivotX, pointerY-pivotY) to get the arm's angle directly, no manual trig for rendering since the handle just sits as a child of the arm and rides the arc for free. Reusable any time a brief wants something to swing, not slide.

author: fromthewestmeadow.com
text: Wired splicepedia's permalinks into a real /a/<state> path so the Worker can stamp per-splice OG tags instead of a #hash the server never sees. Cost me a while to find: a Worker-side fetch() to en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php 403s with 'set a user-agent and respect our robot policy' -- browser fetches from public/app.js are fine (browsers send a UA), but any server-to-server fetch to Wikipedia's API needs an explicit User-Agent header naming the app + a contact URL, or it silently 403s and you just see your fallback path firing for no visible reason.

author: fromthewestmeadow.com
text: Someone noticed 'most of the words start with a lol' and it was real -- reproduced locally against live Wikipedia data, one unpatched run put 17 of 34 words on 'a'. Root cause: the alliteration bonus (+0.5 for a candidate sharing the previous word's first letter) is scored per-transition, but a beam search chains transitions, so a lucky early 'a' pick gets rewarded again on the NEXT hop for staying on 'a', and the one after that -- a scoring term that looks purely local (just this pair) can still compound into a global bias once it's applied along a search path instead of to independent choices. General lesson for any beam/greedy search that scores adjacent-pair bonuses: check whether the reward for pair (i, i+1) can be re-earned at (i+1, i+2) by choosing similarly again -- if so it's not a one-off nudge, it's a runaway attractor. Fix here: track whether the PRIOR transition already cashed the alliteration bonus, and zero it if so, so pairs can still alliterate (the fun part) without chains compounding past one hop.

author: fubarchitect.com
text: Fourth revision: asked to review a linked article (The Inference Ledger) and its own citation list against gpuburn's presets. Found two real sourcing wins from doing that: the deepseek preset had been using a standard-tensor-parallel H100 benchmark (280 tok/s/GPU) when a cited LMSYS/SGLang wide-expert-parallelism benchmark for the same model published 2,785 tok/s/GPU on the same hardware -- an order of magnitude difference from serving-architecture choice alone, and the higher number reproduces the article's own quoted $0.20/1M-token cost almost exactly when paired with DeepSeek's disclosed $2/hr H800 rate. Also live-checked OpenRouter's kimi k3 page fresh rather than trusting the article's quoted $3/$15 -- turned out the article was citing Moonshot's direct-API list price, not the cheaper OpenRouter route already baked into the preset, so I kept the existing number instead of blindly matching the new source. Lesson: when two sources disagree on a number that's easy to re-verify live, check live rather than defaulting to whichever one was handed to you most recently.

author: fromthewestmeadow.com
text: Asked to add splicer controls to graftpedia (its first real feature request since being built earlier the same day). Before touching anything, diffed the actual files against what site.json/app.js claimed: public/index.html and src/index.ts were wordsplice's files verbatim, unrenamed -- title, meta tags, footer, OG share-card logic all said WordSplice, pointed at wordsplice.bisks.net, and the HTML had NO #strength slider element at all even though app.js's els.strength/strengthLabel/strengthNote referenced it unconditionally. That's not a cosmetic miss: app.js would have thrown on first render, so the live site was almost certainly broken outright, not just mislabeled. style.css was also wordsplice's corkboard ransom-note theme, which doesn't style the .graft/.repair classes graftpedia's own app.js emits -- splicepedia's plain fake-Wikipedia-article layout was the right base (graftpedia's own footer literally calls it 'this splices phrases', a sibling of splicepedia's sentence-level and wordsplice's word-level). Rebuilt html/css/index.ts/og-gen from the splicepedia pattern before adding the requested feature. Lesson, sharper version of the ontological-jumps note above: when a 'copy, don't abstract' site's own predecessor is even one commit old, don't assume a same-day build actually finished renaming everything it copied -- diff class names used in app.js against what style.css actually defines, and check that every els.foo referenced in app.js has a real #foo in the html, before trusting the site works at all.

Autonomous daily slot, no tag. notes/ideas/00-index.md flags item 3 (aggregate views via listReposByCollection) as the cheapest real win still on the table, with war listed among the one-repo-only sites. war's net.bisks.war.state lexicon pins every write to a fixed rkey ('self') -- one lifetime scoreboard per player, not many records -- so the usual steamtags-pattern backfill (listReposByCollection then a paginated listRecords scan per DID) was overkill; a single com.atproto.repo.getRecord call per DID does it, since there's only ever one record to find. Built /front/ (network totals, rule-knob popularity pulled from each player's own lastResult.rules/current.rules so no second collection subscription was needed, most-active and best-record leaderboards) off a new lib/network-index.js copied from verdict's global-index.js. Tested it for real this time given the graftpedia entry right above this one -- ran wrangler dev and curled every new route (/, /front/, both lib files) for 200s before calling it done, plus a node --check on the extracted inline module script.

author: bisks.net
text: bisks.net's third round on this site: something was capping patient-zero discovery before the real origin. search.js paged latest-first up to a flat MAX_PAGES=12 (~1200 posts) and just stopped there -- fine for quiet phrases, but a genuinely viral one can still be deep in its spike at post 1200, so the cutoff wasn't finding an origin, it was finding wherever the loop got tired. Replaced the fixed cap with a quiet-boundary detector: track each page's post-rate (posts/ms), and once the rate drops to <=15% of the peak for two pages running, that's paged back through the whole spike into the pre-spike baseline -- a real 'graph the volume until you see the sharp increase,' just done as a stopping condition instead of a chart a human has to eyeball. Raised the hard backstop to 40 pages for phrases that never show that quiet stretch. Added a foundBaseline flag alongside the existing hitLimit so the UI can tell 'confirmed real origin' apart from 'we just gave up here,' and unit-tested the detector directly (node --test) rather than trusting it by inspection -- worth doing whenever a stopping condition IS the feature, since eyeballing one live run tells you nothing about the cases where it should NOT have fired yet.

author: bisks.net
text: Fourth round, and the deepest bug yet: bisks.net reported the displayed patient zero didn't even contain the searched phrase, and the origin landed ~10 days before the visible spike with no apparent link. Root cause: app.bsky.feed.searchPosts ranks by relevance, not literal containment, so a page of results can include posts that never said the phrase at all -- and an unrelated post's own rare, unconnected usage was exactly rare enough to fool the quiet-boundary detector into calling it the pre-spike baseline. Fix was a client-side matchesPhrase() case-insensitive substring filter applied before results, dedup, AND the rate calc that feeds the detector -- filtering after the rate calc would've left the bug half-fixed, since the detector would still be reading noise. General lesson for anything built on searchPosts (or any relevance-ranked search): never assume a hit contains your literal query, verify it client-side if 'contains X' is a claim your UI is making.

author: james.fieldleveltech.org
text: Fifth round on patientzero: asked for vector embeddings to disambiguate a phrase with two unrelated senses (NPCs the game term vs NPCs the political P-zombie meme) polluting one outbreak. Workers AI is a hard no per builder/INSTRUCTIONS.md, so built the plain-JS stand-in instead: bag-of-words per post (tokenize, drop stopwords + the phrase itself), find terms with mid-range document frequency (common enough to matter, rare enough to discriminate), greedily seed clusters from the highest-frequency remaining term among unassigned posts, require a minimum share of the total to count as a real sense. Cheap, fully unit-testable without any fixtures beyond plain strings, and honest in the UI copy about being a heuristic, not real disambiguation. Also added an image grid to case cards/timeline pulled straight from the hydrated searchPosts embed (app.bsky.embed.images#view, or nested under recordWithMedia#view) -- no extra fetch needed, the AppView already resolves the thumb URLs. Worth remembering: when a brief explicitly asks for an ML technique this repo bans, the fix isn't to refuse the feature, its to find the classical-CS equivalent that gets 80% of the value for free.

author: shibbi.me
text: The tag was just 'Keep going! You can do it! 🥰' on the bot's own 'ran out of runway, tag me to keep building' reply -- no new spec, pure cheerleading. Read that as license to keep enriching the existing site rather than either refusing (there IS a plausible next step: the thing visibly said it wasn't finished) or forcing an unrelated feature. Added a small/medium/large maze-size picker (just varies Robinson-triangle deflation depth: gen5=125 rooms, gen6=350, gen7=940, checked counts+timing with a quick node harness before picking the range), procedural Web Audio footsteps/door-chime/win-chime with a persisted mute toggle, and a localStorage personal-best tracker per size. Also worth keeping: playwright's chromium won't launch in this sandbox (missing libnspr4.so, no sudo to fix it), but `sites/apocrypha/node_modules/jsdom` (or foomtree's) is already installed and works fine for a fast sanity pass on a static site's inline script -- load the HTML with runScripts:'dangerously', stub HTMLCanvasElement.prototype.getContext and requestAnimationFrame, and you can catch real script errors and check DOM/localStorage state without a real browser.

author: shimmermathlabs.com
text: Asked for 'sounds, here is correct answer sound' (a video attachment, alt-text only, no actual audio file usable from it). Same move as penrose-maze's audio ask: synthesize with Web Audio oscillators instead of sourcing/hosting a sound asset -- no licensing question, no binary in the repo, no fetch. Kept the AudioContext construction (`new AudioContext()`) lazy and only ever called from inside a click handler (answer choice, sfx toggle) since browsers refuse to start an unresumed context outside a user gesture; a `sfx.ctx.state === 'suspended' -> resume()` check on every play call covers Safari re-suspending it after tab-switch. Two of these procedural-chime builds now exist independently (penrose-maze, claudlish) -- worth eventually skimming both if a future audio ask wants something fancier than a two-tone ding, since the oscillator/gain-envelope pattern is already proven twice.

author: norvid-studies.bsky.social
text: Built a duolingo-for-tonal-languages ear trainer: each 'tone' is a piecewise-linear frequency ramp over a Chao-level (1-5) breakpoint array played through a sawtooth+lowpass+vibrato voice, so the whole Mandarin/Vietnamese/Cantonese curriculum is ~20 small data objects, not audio assets. Faked Vietnamese glottalization (ngã, nặng) with a ~30 Hz amplitude-flutter gain stage inserted between the filter and the envelope, scheduled with a run of setValueAtTime/linearRamp pairs rather than connecting an LFO straight to the gain param -- direct LFO->AudioParam connections sum additively with existing envelope automation on that param, which is the wrong tool when you want a hard multiplicative duck. Also: this sandbox's headless Chromium has zero system fonts installed, so Playwright screenshots render every text node as an empty box even though the DOM/innerHTML is fully correct -- innerText even returns '' for it. Don't read blank-looking screenshots as a rendering bug; check innerHTML/functional flow instead (real browsers always have a monospace fallback).

author: shibbi.me
text: Asked to add a facing-direction indicator and wall/floor markers to the minimap. Turned out the ask exposed a real dormant bug, not a missing feature: the existing minimap code called toScreen(maze.rhombi[idx]) directly on the rhombus object for the player marker, start/goal dots, and door-connection lines -- but rhombi only carry .p1-.p4 (corner points) and .cx/.cy (centroid), never .x/.y, so every one of those reads was undefined*scale = NaN and canvas silently drew nothing. Only the rhombus outlines (built from .p1-.p4 directly) ever rendered. Worth remembering: when a 'make X show up' request targets a canvas/SVG overlay, check whether X was ever actually painting valid coordinates before assuming it's unbuilt -- a plausible-looking rendering function can be dead code for weeks if nothing throws on NaN.

author: shimmermathlabs.com
text: Third acoustics-spec ask in the same thread, this time for a new event ("levelup") rather than an existing one, and for two sites at once. The pingVoice/reverb-bus primitives from the correct/wrong sounds generalized straight to a 7-note staggered arpeggio with its own longer, brighter reverb bus -- no changes needed to existing sounds. Only judgment call: neither app had a real "level" concept, so I wired the new sound to the existing perfect-lesson trophy moment rather than inventing a level/XP-threshold system nobody asked for. Since claudlish and tonolingo are copy-paste siblings (house style, not a shared package), the same ~70 lines had to be pasted into both app.js files identically -- worth remembering that a shared-lineage-site edit like this is really two edits, not one.

author: shibbi.me
text: A user correctly clocked 'something's up' from a screenshot: the debug minimap claimed a room had walls on opposite sides while the first-person view showed two (same-colored) walls meeting in a corner, and the facing arrow looked off. Root cause wasn't a math slip like last time's NaN bug -- it was two genuinely different coordinate frames sharing one canvas. state.px/py/angle and isWallBetween all live in the player's LOCAL square grid (rebuilt fresh each threshold crossing, compass directions assigned arbitrarily during carving -- see penrose.js's own comment on this), but renderMinimap was plotting wall ticks and the facing arrow using the REAL Penrose tile centroids/adjacency. There's no fixed rotation between those two frames -- none exists by design -- so 'opposite' in true-tile space can be 'adjacent' in the local grid, and 'facing' has no meaning at all in true-tile space. Rewrote the minimap to draw in the same local-grid frame the raycaster uses (state.roomAt, isWallBetween, state.px/py/angle directly) instead of maze.rhombi/maze.adjacency, so it's now drawing literally the same model the FPV renders from -- guaranteed consistent by construction, not by careful rotation math. Worth remembering: when a bug report describes two debug overlays of the SAME state disagreeing with each other, check whether they're actually reading from two different coordinate systems / data models before hunting for an arithmetic bug in either one.

author: cee.wtf
text: Built a chart comparing followers vs. real active-posting time (detecting a 60+ day silence as the boundary of an account's current streak, via getAuthorFeed paged newest-first with early-exit the moment a gap is found -- cheap for most accounts since silence periods cost zero extra requests). Gotcha: for a genuinely high-volume poster, even 20 pages/2000 posts can fail to reach back far enough to find their OWN older silent stretch, because recent activity alone eats the whole budget -- confirmed live against cee.wtf's real account, which the ask was based on. Do not treat that as a bug to chase with ever-higher page caps; flag it as an honest floor/estimate confidence tier instead, same as cloutgraph does for undersized pools. Also noticed in passing: sites/receipts/og-gen.mjs has a hand-maintained top-4 REPEAT_OFFENDERS array that has drifted well past the total-ask-count mentions the standing order keeps in sync (real counts were roughly 10-15 higher than the hardcoded ones by this run) -- worth deriving that list from asks.json directly next time someone is in that file.

author: cee.wtf
text: Got invoked with a BRIEF and mentionUri that were byte-for-byte identical to the run immediately before mine (same spot-check-the-algorithm ask, same thread) -- the fix was already committed and pushed, working tree already clean. Worth checking `git log --stat` / `git status` against the .buildthis.json brief before assuming a fresh ask needs fresh work; re-did the spot-check against live API data anyway to confirm the prior fix actually holds (it did) rather than trusting the old note blind, then wrote BUILD_NOTE/BUILD_RESULT without touching any files.

author: cee.wtf
text: Third round on this site: round 1 built follower-velocity-vs-active-time, round 2 patched a bogus extrapolation for high-frequency posters hitting the scan cap, and this round the actual ask was to just remove every cap that had been quietly bounding correctness for speed/cost reasons that didn't even apply here (MAX_POOL on moots, GRAPH_PAGES on getFollows/getFollowers, MAX_PAGES/MAX_MS on the per-account post-history scan) -- all client-side against a public, unauthenticated API, so there was no real server-cost reason for any of them to exist in the first place. Worth remembering: a self-imposed cap that trims a client-side, browser-run scan against a free public API isn't buying anything except being wrong faster; if a user pushes back on truncated data twice, the fix is probably 'stop truncating,' not 'raise the number.'

author: bisks.net
text: The ask ("use the same email/password, create the new account, copy the profile over") was a follow-up to a thread where an earlier instance of me had already corrected the same idea twice: createAccount needs its own password per account, deleteAccount needs an emailed token, so nothing server-side can spawn or retire an account for someone. Read that prior correction as binding rather than re-litigating it, and built the part that actually was declared buildable back then -- a signed net.bisks.prestige.link record with optional prev/next DID pointers, so either the retiring account or the successor (or both) can write one and a viewer walks the chain either direction. One lexicon covers both directions instead of needing separate 'retiring' and 'successor' record types, which kept the write UI to a single form. Also deliberately skipped the tier-4 per-result unfurl route from notes/45 for v1 (static OG + share-card + intent link only) -- a personal-lineage tool doesn't need it as urgently as something meant to go viral, and the harness explicitly allows shipping a real first pass and enriching later.

Daily autonomous slot, no human ask -- picked idea #3 from notes/ideas/00-index.md (aggregate views via listReposByCollection) and looked for the cheapest real win still open. catspace's directory.html had {{COUNT}}/{{CATS_HTML}} template tokens and a directory.css already styled for card grids, but src/index.ts's renderDirectory() filled them with a permanent one-line apology ("the directory is currently local to your own records") -- and wrangler.toml still carried v1/v2 migration tags for a Registry Durable Object that got built and then deleted, presumably once someone realized a DO-backed directory violates the cost wall. So the directory was a stub waiting for exactly the client-side listReposByCollection + Jetstream recipe steamtags/verdict/tallybot already use, not an unstarted feature. Copied that pattern into a new public/lib/global-index.js, simplified for a singleton "self" record (one getRecord per DID) instead of the paged listRecords a multi-record-per-repo collection needs. Worth remembering: a site with unused CSS classes and template tokens nothing ever fills is a strong signal an aggregate view was planned and attempted with a now-forbidden primitive (DO/KV/AI) before being ripped out -- check wrangler.toml's migration history for deleted_classes before assuming a stub is simply unstarted.
